title: Orsen and the Terminal
premise: Sable Whitlock, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs supply routes between two fleets that severed contact decades ago—until gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, exposing the hidden relay that keeps their silence intact. Hunted by both sides, Sable discovers the flicker was Earth's last transmission loop dying, and the lie they've maintained—that each fleet betrayed the other—is the only thing preventing war. To end it, Sable must broadcast the truth of Earth's fall to both fleets at once, sacrificing their anonymity, their garden, and possibly their life. In the final chapter, the fleets stand down not because they forgive, but because grief, finally shared, is heavier than vengeance.
about_author: Hazel Halloran is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction, and her work is known for its patient, ecological attention to machines and landscapes alike. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps a failing greenhouse she refuses to give up on.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While tending the orbital garden and running contraband messages between the silent fleets, Sable experiences the nine-second gravity flicker—and realizes their hidden relay station lit up on every sensor in the system. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a life built on invisibility cracking open in less time than a breath.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and Idris Vane, a fleet investigator sent to find the relay's operator. Sable races to preserve the false war-logs proving mutual betrayal, while Idris uncovers evidence the flicker came from Earth itself. The beat is mounting paranoia: hunter and hunted circling the same terrible question—who benefits from the silence?

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. Cornered at the relay as both fleets converge, Sable decrypts the dying transmission loop: Earth fell years ago, and the fleets' founders knew, manufacturing the betrayal lie to keep their people fighting instead of grieving. Sable broadcasts everything—the truth, the garden, their own name—to every ship at once. The beat is furious, terrified resolve.

chapters.title: What Grief Weighs
chapters.summary: Idris's POV, resolution. Weapons armed on both sides hold fire as the truth spreads through the fleets; Idris chooses not to arrest Sable but to testify alongside them. The novel closes with Sable returning to the garden, now tended by hands from both fleets, planting for people who may never come. The beat is hard-won, imperfect peace.
